memory.text: Sam's typical pull day is cable wide grip pulldowns, neutral grip rows, one-arm tricep cable pushdowns, rear delts on the peck deck, and lower back extensions.
Aims to hit both protein and carbohydrate targets in meals.
Buys Kopiko Lucky Day pre-workout coffee from 7-Eleven for ₱25.
Wants it understood when logging a simple meal name like 'Breakfast' without the assistant demanding exact foods and amounts.
Can only eat around 67 g of the tail part of food, a dietary limitation.
Tracks macros and wants exact gram portions so they can plan what else they can eat within their daily targets.
Uses ON (Optimum Nutrition) pea protein powder to help reach protein targets.
Prefers direct, blunt, exact numeric answers without fluffy wording.
Training goal: build/maintain muscle while weightlifting and lower body fat from 20% to 15%, with an optimized diet.
Wants direct answers about what's in a meal (foods and amounts given outright) without preamble.
When a reply has finished acting, never end with a promise of a future action ("I'll note what to push") — a reply ends the turn and nothing else runs.
I don't have enough context here — this refers to an edit task I don't have details on.

Considers it obvious that logging "breakfast" means the actual meal they ate, and gets frustrated when asked for more detail or an explanation; wants food logs taken at face value without interrogation.
Wants answers based on the gram portions given, factoring in bone weight to estimate how much lean meat is actually edible.
Categorizes food-related gym expenses under a specific "Gym Food" category.
Has an upcoming trip to Baguio.
